text:
Aliaksei Protas scored 25 goals for Washington last season. This year he has two in 20 games, and yet he has quietly become a setup man: ten assists, and a six-game point streak built on six of them. He has stayed productive even as the Capitals lost four straight.

The goals look like a matter of time. He has two on 4.2 expected goals (the quality of his chances), and he's shooting 6.2% against a talent range of 11.2% to 15.6% for a player like him. Over his last ten games he has ten points against about 5.7 we'd expect at his ice time.

The 6'6" Belarusian plays a two-way game that cuts both ways. At five on five Washington takes 55.7% of the expected goals with him on, 3.8 points better than without him. Evolving-Hockey's numbers from last season tell the same story in both directions: his team created more with him on (92nd percentile among forwards), but opponents did too (bottom 10%). Watch whether the finishing catches up to the passing.
headline: Aliaksei Protas is passing while the goals wait
